section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how the two interpretations of "He redeems in peace My soul" are connected, showing that the redemption from Above is elevated through the actions of man.
section.t: And based on this, the connection between the two explanations of "He redeems in peace My soul" will be understood

[the simple explanation that "He redeems" etc. refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, and the explanation of our Sages that "He redeems" etc. refers to the person who engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation],
for this—that the Holy One, blessed be He redeems Israel—
[even to the matter in its simple sense,
that even during the time of exile, behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps86,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, guards Israel both spiritually and physically,
so that no thing should be able to touch them, G-d forbid,
and as is explained in detail in the Psalm "He who dwells in the shelter"87.
And even that
(afterwards)
He will redeem Israel from the exile]
is brought about through man
(through his service in the three lines),
"He redeemed me for me and for my sons."
And through this,
the redemption from Above
(the first explanation of "He redeems in peace")
is in a manner more elevated than it is in and of itself.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates on the concept of being "occupied" with Torah, kindness, and prayer, explaining how this brings peace to all aspects of the soul and the world.
section.t: A)
And it emphasizes "all who engage in Torah" etc.,
that his service in Torah
(and acts of kindness and prayer)
is in the manner of "occupation"88.
For just as a businessman is busy and occupied with this all day,
even at a time when he is not engaged in the body and essence of his business,
so too is the matter of one who is occupied with Torah,
that he is occupied with this throughout the entire day
(even when not during his study time),
meaning that even when he deals with mundane matters, he does so for the sake of Heaven89
and even in the manner of "know Him"90,
that even at the time of his involvement in physical matters, he is occupied with matters of
(knowledge of Havayah)
Torah91.
And through this, "He redeems in peace My soul" is brought about,
peace in all matters
(and faculties)
of his soul,
peace in the supernal retinue and peace in the lower retinue92
[and these two matters also exist in the soul of man93
[even to the point that there is peace in its perfection between the created and the Creator,
that Israel becomes
(through the Torah)
and the Holy One, blessed be He, one entity94],
and also in his portion in the world.
For in addition to the fact that worldly matters do not prevent him from serving G-d,
rather they themselves agree and assist,
for "many are with me,"
that even the sparks of holiness stand with immense yearning
(and pray)
that they be refined,
similar to the matter of "for many are with me" in its simple sense,
that even the men of Avshalom prayed95
for the victory of Dovid.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the dual meaning of "in peace" as peace from Above downward and from below upward, corresponding to Torah, kindness, and prayer.
section.t: And it says "He redeems in peace,"
"in peace" is two peaces
(similar to what is explained in Torah Or, discourse "And I will return in peace to my father's house"96),
peace from Above downward,
the drawing down from Above downward through Torah and mitzvos,
and peace from below upward,
the service of teshuvah,
until the teshuvah of "and the spirit shall return to G-d who gave it"—the soul in the body
(for length of days and good years),
and even while he is in the body, he is in the aspect of "and the spirit shall return" etc.,
and in the manner of "you shall see your world in your life"97.
And these two modes are connected to the three lines of Torah, acts of kindness, and prayer
(in a congregation),
Torah and acts of kindness are a drawing down from Above downward,
and prayer is an elevation from below upward.
